tag: Episode 28 Side Story · A Promise at the Rainy Bus Stop
title: A Promise at the Rainy Bus Stop

beats.t: At three in the afternoon, the forecast proved accurate. The classroom windows suddenly darkened, and a downpour began.
(She said not to go to the stop. But I have to catch a bus to get home.)
Yeoni opened the taped umbrella. Its ribs stood crooked. But it opened.
Can't get home without the bus stop, Ms. Neighbor. Thanks for worrying, though.
Inside the wallet in their bag, the folded talisman grew faintly warm. Yeoni did not notice.
In the hallway, classmates cried that they had no umbrellas. The convenience store had already sold out.
This is all I've got. Two ribs held with tape. Anyone sharing has to accept getting half soaked.
Nobody raised a hand. Everyone laughed at the crooked umbrella. Yeoni laughed with them.
(Still a pretty good umbrella. Repaired things are all right.)
The bus stop roof sheltered a crowd. Rain hammered the asphalt white.
(Here I am. Nothing's happening. Scared myself for nothing.)
The display showed seven minutes until the bus. Yeoni shook out the umbrella and stepped beneath the roof.
Then the talisman in their wallet grew unmistakably hot. Yeoni opened the bag. The crescent on the folded paper glowed very faintly.
Why is Yundal's talisman... Is something here?
At the roof's edge, on the boundary of falling rain, stood someone in a black coat. But today, no umbrella.
Ms. Neighbor? What are you doing there?
Her hair was soaked. Water streamed from her coat's shoulders. The umbrella she carried every clear day was nowhere.
Where's your umbrella? You always carry it when it's sunny.
I gave it to the playground child earlier. They were alone in the rain.
The bandage kid? But what about you?
I can get wet. I'm used to it.
Yeoni did not think. Before thought, their hand moved. They tilted the umbrella halfway over the woman.
Let's share. We'll both get half wet, though.
At that moment, something overlapped in their mind. The same stop. The same rain. Their own hand tilting an umbrella. And someone whose face was erased.
(This... the scene in the library. The person then was...)
The face would not come. Only the face of the person beneath the umbrella was white and empty, as though rubbed out with an eraser.
The woman lifted her head and looked straight at Yeoni. Her eyes were red. Whether from rain, Yeoni could not tell.
...How much is this?
What? How much is what?
Sharing your umbrella. How much? What do I give you?
A strange question. Yet she truly waited for an answer. Like someone unable to receive anything without a price tag.
It's free. Why charge someone when it's raining?
Her shoulders collapsed. Her breath caught. She covered her mouth. Water flowed over the back of her hand.
Are you okay? Does something hurt?
I've heard those words before. A very long time ago. At the same bus stop.
From me?
No. Not you. It can't be you. You don't remember.
It was neither an answer nor a confession. Closer to speaking to herself.
It's okay not to remember. We're sharing now. This belongs to now.
She looked at Yeoni for a long time. Thin rain passed between them. One umbrella rib trembled in the wind.
Belongs to now. I didn't know there was such a thing. I thought everything had to be repaid.
Think about repayment later. Staying dry comes first. Well, half dry.
The bus pulled in with a spray of water. People lined up. Yeoni looked at the woman.
Come with me. Same apartment building.
Go ahead. I'll take the next one.
Then keep the umbrella. I can run after I get off.
Yeoni placed the taped handle in her hand. She could neither release it nor properly hold it.
The bus departed. The stop receded outside the window. Without opening the umbrella, the woman crouched, holding it to her chest. Her shoulders shook.
Yeoni reached the apartment completely soaked. Water pooled on the corridor floor. A package sat before the neighbor's door.
Today, the label faced up. Yeoni had not meant to look. It simply caught their eye.
[ Recipient · Seo Hanbi ]
(Seo Hanbi. Hanbi. ...Cold rain.)
Cold rain. Rain was in her name. Umbrellas on clear days, rain scent on clear days. Even her name was rain.
(Says a name is a debt, then leaves it written on packages like this.)
Yeoni almost laughed. But instead, their chest hurt. They remembered the shoulders collapsing at the stop.
Inside, Neo offered a towel. Instead of asking what had happened, he took the wet bag first.
“That woman again. Stronger smell this time. Rain and tears.”
Yes. She cried. I shared my umbrella, and she asked how much.
Neo said nothing for a while. His finger pressed the folded towel's edge.
“...I know someone who asks how much. Over there.”
I think I know, too. But don't tell me yet. I want to figure it out.
“Why solve it yourself? Faster if I tell you.”
If you tell me, it's your memory. I need to figure it out to believe it. She'll need that to believe it, too.
Instead of answering, Neo sat beside Yeoni. Their wet shoulders touched, but he did not move away. They stayed like that until Yeoni spoke first.
“...Still stubborn. That's a relief.”
At the same time, beyond the wall, an umbrella stood open to dry in the unlit room. Crooked ribs wrapped in tape.
Seo Hanbi sat beside it and opened the ledger. Yeoni's entry. Beneath the uncollected line, a new line spread.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Uncollected: 2 ]
She stared at the number for a long time. One more thing she could not repay.
The golden cord tightened at the wrist holding the pen. Pain burrowed into flesh. She made no sound.
Instead, she took a folded note from her coat's inner pocket and laid it on her palm. The drumming child's name. She folded it once more to keep it dry.
